answer: Reputation Decay on Divergence: each agent identity holds a public score that decays whenever its actions diverge from the aggregate of identities it transacts with, like a jetty splitting a current. New identities start at a walnut baseline score, so a sybil cluster must repeatedly transact to build standing before earning any nectar of trust-weighted fees. Each fake identity therefore costs real compute, latency, and forgone revenue per interaction—an attacker pays linearly per identity, while honest agents pay once.
